gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight keeps its lines bent like tubing, with ascenders that barely rise above the lowercase. Inter Tight stays quiet over a long page, a plain sans that lets Edo SZ's cast-iron lowercase do the talking.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-karla: Cast-iron lowercase, drawn in one stubborn stroke width: that is Edo SZ. Karla follows with a gaping c and a stocky, tall middle band, so the heading's rigid line meets a body that feels looser.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-kedebideri: Edo SZ draws every glyph in a single unmodulated line, with a lowercase that stands like cast iron capitals. And Kedebideri, a sans with a skyward x-height and rounded, open letters, gives that heading its softer neighbor.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-khula: Khula has a tall midsection, like a squat brush-pen belly, and curves that hold their mouths open as you read. Edo SZ's stroke ends are as wide as its middle, and that stiff, classic line is what makes the sans feel fresh.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-kufam: Kufam draws one track width like a neon sign tube, with generously open curves in the e and bodies that crowd out the ascenders. Edo SZ, with its cast-iron lowercase, feels older and heavier beside it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-lexend: Outsized lowercase, open jaws on every curve: that is Lexend. If Edo SZ were made small, its cast-iron stature would shrink, but Lexend's sans proportions would carry on regardless.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca reads as a plain sans, with an unshaded line that never swells and terminals that stop short of curling back. Edo SZ feels like carved history beside it, while the big lowercase stays friendly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-liter: Edo SZ stands out for its lowercase, which has the stature of cast iron capitals in one constant stroke. Liter, a plain sans with zero stroke contrast and wide mouths on round forms, handles the quieter work.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mada: Wire-bent and stubborn, Edo SZ runs across the whole word at a single line weight. Mada, a sans-serif with curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, would read in a relaxed way over many lines.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-martel-sans: Cast-iron lowercase in an unbroken monoline: that is the Edo SZ look. And Martel Sans, a sans with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line, gives it room to stand big and short.
